mainTopic: Evening קריאת שמע: the חצות fence, joining גאולה to ערבית, the value of אשרי, and the bedtime שמע
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's question about the חכמים, who say evening קריאת שמע must be said by חצות. The answer is that they agree with רבן גמליאל that the Torah allows it all night, but they made חצות a fence (סייג). A ברייתא explains why: so a tired worker will go straight to שמע and תפלה instead of eating and falling asleep. The ברייתא's harsh warning of death gets two explanations: the real danger of sleep, or teaching that ערבית is a חובה. The ברייתא's order, שמע and then תפלה, supports רבי יוחנן, who praises joining גאולה to the evening תפלה. רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees, and the גמרא explains the dispute through both סברא and the פסוק ״בשכבך ובקומך״, then defends רבי יוחנן from the challenge of השכיבנו. Next come teachings about אשרי (תהלה לדוד), why it lacks a נ verse, and the speed of מיכאל, גבריאל and other heavenly messengers. The amud ends with רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule to say שמע again in bed, a supporting verse, and the start of רב נחמן's comment, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the חכמים hold like רבן גמליאל, why not say so?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. If the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל that the מצוה lasts all night, why do they say only until חצות?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they hold like רבן גמליאל, then let them say the same thing as רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of a question. Just before this, the גמרא showed that the חכמים cannot hold like רבי אליעזר. Now it shows they cannot simply hold like רבן גמליאל either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל says evening שמע may be said until dawn (עמוד השחר). If the חכמים agree with him about the Torah law, their ruling should also say until dawn. Their ruling of חצות seems to match neither opinion, so it looks like it needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold / that is their opinion
the Tanna who says evening שמע may be said until dawn

phrases.english: And if they hold like Rabban Gamliel
phrases.notes: רבן גמליאל: 'when you lie down' (בשכבך) means the whole night, until dawn.

phrases.english: let them say like Rabban Gamliel (until dawn).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל סְבִירָא לְהוּ לֵימְרוּ כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question started earlier on the daf (the רבי אליעזר side came on the previous amud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל, their stated time limit should match his (dawn). Their different wording suggests a different opinion that has no clear source.

steps.title: They agree with רבן גמליאל, but חצות is a protective limit
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים really do hold like רבן גמליאל on the Torah level. They said חצות only to keep people far from sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really they hold like רבן גמליאל. The reason they said 'until midnight' is to keep a person far away from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The חכמים agree that the Torah allows שמע all night. They set an earlier deadline as a safety measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two things: what the Torah allows (until dawn) and what the חכמים require in practice (until חצות). The earlier deadline is a rabbinic protection. It does not argue with רבן גמליאל about the Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: really / in truth (introduces an answer that keeps the original assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים argue with רבן גמליאל here. In this answer they fully agree with him about the Torah law. חצות is only their added safety limit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic pattern: the Torah's time window and the rabbinic time window can differ, and the rabbinic one is a fence around the Torah one.

phrases.english: Really, they hold like Rabban Gamliel,
and the fact that they say 'until midnight'

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי לְהַרְחִיק אֶת הָאָדָם מִן הָעֲבֵירָה.
phrases.english: is in order to keep a person far from sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing Torah-level law from a rabbinic protective decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים's 'until חצות' was taken as their view of the Torah law, which would contradict רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל about the Torah law. חצות is only a rabbinic fence to prevent missing שמע.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the חכמים' fence and the danger it prevents
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the answer. The חכמים made a fence so a tired worker would not put off שמע, fall asleep, and miss it completely. Instead he goes straight to shul, learns, davens, and only then eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The חכמים made a fence around their words. They did not want a person to come home from the field in the evening and say, 'I'll go home, eat a little, drink a little, sleep a little, and then say שמע and daven.' Then sleep overtakes him and he sleeps the whole night. Instead, a person coming from the field in the evening goes into the בית הכנסת. If he usually reads תנ״ך, he reads. If he usually learns משנה, he learns. Then he says שמע and davens, and afterwards he eats his bread and makes a ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof that the חכמים made a protective fence for קריאת שמע. The ברייתא shows the exact problem the fence is meant to stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger is a person who knows he has all night and keeps pushing off שמע until he falls asleep. With an earlier deadline of חצות, he feels pressure to do it right away. So he davens first and eats afterward. The ברייתא backs up the idea from step 2 that חצות is a fence, not the Torah's limit.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught (in a baraita)
and sleep grabs him / overtakes him

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is a source for the practice of davening מעריב before eating dinner, so you don't push it off and forget.

phrases.english: As it was taught: the Sages made a fence for their words,
so that a person should not
come from the field in the evening,
and say: 'I will go to my house
and eat a little and drink a little,
and sleep a little,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אֶקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְאֶתְפַּלֵּל״,
phrases.english: and afterwards I will recite Shema and pray,'
and sleep overtakes him
and he ends up sleeping the whole night.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה בָּעֶרֶב,
phrases.english: Rather, a person comes from the field in the evening,
phrases.notes: Because of the midnight deadline, he worries about missing it and acts right away.

phrases.english: goes into the synagogue,
if he is used to reading Scripture, he reads;
and if he is used to learning Mishnah, he learns,
and he recites Shema and prays,
and then eats his bread and makes a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'until חצות' is a rabbinic fence
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the חכמים made a סייג for קריאת שמע so people would not delay and fall asleep

steps.title: The ברייתא's warning: breaking the words of the חכמים deserves death
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a severe warning. Whoever breaks the words of the חכמים is חייב מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anyone who goes against the words of the חכמים deserves death.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the same ברייתא. It sets up the גמרא's next question about why such a harsh warning appears here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives very strong backing to the rabbinic fence it just described. This is not a death penalty given by a court. It means death at the hands of Heaven. The harshness is surprising, and that is what the גמרא asks about next.

keyTerms.meaning: liable to death (at the hands of Heaven)

phrases.english: And anyone who transgresses the words of the Sages
is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָל הָעוֹבֵר עַל דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים חַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final line of the ברייתא quoted in step 3. It is separated out because the next question targets it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking the words of the חכמים, here the fence of saying שמע before חצות, makes a person חייב מיתה.

steps.title: Why is the death penalty mentioned only here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes this rabbinic rule different. Other rabbinic rules carry no warning of death, so why does this one?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different everywhere else, where it does not say 'deserves death,' and what is different here, where it does say 'deserves death'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the harsh warning and asks why it appears specifically about קריאת שמע. Steps 6 and 7 give two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים make many rules, and most do not come with a death warning. Nothing about this particular fence looks more serious than the others. So the גמרא wants to know what special reason the ברייתא had for using such strong language here.

phrases.english: What is different in every other place
that it does not teach 'liable to death,'
and what is different here
that it does teach 'liable to death'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בְּכָל דּוּכְתָּא דְּלָא קָתָנֵי חַיָּיב מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the unusual wording of the ברייתא's final line in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא attaches a death warning to this rabbinic fence when other rabbinic rules carry no such warning.

steps.title: First answer: the danger of being overcome by sleep
steps.stepSummary: This fence is stricter because a tired person can easily fall asleep and miss שמע completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is because of the danger of being overpowered by sleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from step 5. This rule is treated more harshly because sleep can easily make a person miss the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harsh warning does not mean that breaking this rule is a bigger sin than breaking other rabbinic rules. It comes from the real danger here: a tired worker who lies down 'for a minute' will very likely sleep through the night. Strong words are needed to make the fence actually work.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces one of several possible answers
Being overpowered by sleep, which a person cannot control

phrases.english: If you wish, say
because there is the danger of being overcome by sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִיכָּא אוֹנֶס שֵׁינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why this rabbinic rule carries a death warning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the risk of falling asleep is so high, the fence needs extra force

steps.title: Second answer: teaching that the evening prayer is required
steps.stepSummary: The strong words reject the view that תפלת ערבית is optional and teach that it is a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say it comes to reject the one who says 'the evening prayer is optional.' It teaches us that it is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. The harsh language is there to teach that davening ערבית is an obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some held that ערבית is רשות, meaning optional. The ברייתא includes davening in the worker's evening routine, so its warning shows that ערבית is a חובה. In this answer, the focus moves from the danger of sleep to the status of ערבית itself.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude or reject another opinion

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
to exclude the one who says
"the evening prayer is optional,"
it teaches us that it is mandatory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, alternative answer to the same question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why this rabbinic rule carries a death warning
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To reject the view that ערבית is optional and teach that it is a חובה
steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons for the death warning: (1) the danger of falling asleep, (2) teaching that ערבית is a חובה, not רשות.

steps.title: The ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן on joining גאולה to the evening prayer
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the worker first reads שמע and then davens. This matches רבי יוחנן, who praises joining the גאולה blessing to ערבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'He reads קריאת שמע and davens.' This supports רבי יוחנן. For רבי יוחנן said: Who belongs to the World to Come? One who joins גאולה to the evening תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a detail in the ברייתא: the order of שמע first, then davening. It shows that this detail supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At night the ברייתא puts שמע before תפלה, just like in the morning. רבי יוחנן says the ideal is to go straight from the גאולה blessing after שמע (גאל ישראל) into the evening שמונה עשרה. The ברייתא's order fits his view exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said: quoting an earlier source in order to discuss it
One who has a share in the World to Come
One who joins the redemption blessing directly to שמונה עשרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of not interrupting between גאל ישראל and שמונה עשרה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר, קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמִתְפַּלֵּל.
phrases.english: The Master said: he recites Shema and prays.
This supports Rabbi Yoḥanan.
For Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Who is one destined for the World-to-Come?
It is one who juxtaposes redemption
to the evening prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר קוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמִתְפַּלֵּל מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 3 to draw a new point
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that one should join גאולה to the evening תפלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's order: read שמע, then daven

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the prayers were set in the middle
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that the תפלות were set between the morning שמע and the evening שמע, so at night one davens first and reads שמע afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says: the תפלות were set up in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: An opposing view is presented. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the day's תפלות come in between the two readings of שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning has שמע and then תפלה. Then come מנחה and ערבית, and the evening שמע closes the day. So at night, unlike רבי יוחנן's view, ערבית comes before שמע, and there is no need to join גאולה to תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the middle, here meaning between the two readings of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: 'In the middle' does not mean the middle of שמע. It means the תפלות of the whole day sit between the morning שמע and the evening שמע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says:
The prayers were instituted in the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אוֹמֵר תְּפִלּוֹת בָּאֶמְצַע תִּקְּנוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the view that disagrees with רבי יוחנן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At night, one davens ערבית first and only then reads שמע

steps.title: What is the basis of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the root of the disagreement is between רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why each of them holds his view. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical difference is already clear: does שמע come before or after ערבית? Now the גמרא wants the reason behind each view.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? Asks for the root of an argument

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of the מחלוקת just presented
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for each side's position

steps.title: Either a verse or logic is behind the argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that their argument can be explained either through a פסוק or through a סברא. The details come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is a verse. If you want, say it is logic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an outline of its answer: two possible roots of the argument. This line sets up the detailed explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing has been explained yet. The גמרא is only announcing two paths: a disagreement about how to read a פסוק, or a disagreement about reasoning (סברא). Each path will be spelled out next.

phrases.english: If you wish, say a verse;
if you wish, say logic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 10's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument rests either on a פסוק or on a סברא, explained next

steps.title: The logic explanation: רבי יוחנן says there was redemption at night too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens the סברא explanation. According to רבי יוחנן, the גאולה from מצרים already began at night, even though the complete גאולה only came in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is a matter of logic. רבי יוחנן holds that redemption happened at night too. But the full, complete redemption only came in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its first explanation of the argument, the סברא. It gives רבי יוחנן's view: the גאולה from מצרים already started at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If some גאולה happened at night, then the night has a real connection to גאולה. So it makes sense to say the גאולה blessing right before תפלת ערבית, just like in the morning. That is why רבי יוחנן says to read שמע (with its גאולה blessing) first and then daven.

keyTerms.meaning: Logic or reasoning, as opposed to a source from a פסוק
Redemption; here, the redemption from מצרים and the blessing about it after שמע

steps.confusionAlert: In step 11 the גמרא listed the פסוק first and the סברא second. Here it explains them in the opposite order: סברא first, then פסוק. This is the same two-part answer, just explained in reverse order.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is a matter of logic.
phrases.notes: Opens the first of the two explanations promised in step 11.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan holds:
Redemption happened in the evening as well,
phrases.notes: The night of the Exodus already had some redemption, such as the plague of the firstborn.

phrases.english: but the full-fledged redemption
did not come until the morning.
phrases.notes: The Jews actually left מצרים in the daytime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the סברא half of the two-part answer from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן holds that the night already had real גאולה, so the גאולה blessing should be joined to תפלת ערבית.

steps.title: The logic explanation: רבי יהושע בן לוי says night redemption was not real redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that since the full גאולה only came in the morning, what happened at night does not count as complete גאולה. So there is no need to join the גאולה blessing to תפלת ערבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי holds: since the redemption only came from the morning, the night was not a full redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the סברא. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the night of the Exodus was not a real, complete גאולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אמוראים agree about the history: the full גאולה came in the morning. They disagree about whether the partial night גאולה is enough to tie גאולה to the evening. For רבי יהושע בן לוי it is not enough, so at night there is no need to join גאולה to תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not / it does not count as

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the argument is not about what happened in history. It is about how much weight to give the partial redemption at night.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi holds:
since it only happened from the morning,
it was not a full-fledged redemption at night.
phrases.notes: So the night does not call for joining גאולה to תפלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סָבַר כֵּיוָן דְּלָא הָוְיָא אֶלָּא מִצַּפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the same סברא presented in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds that the night's partial גאולה does not count, so there is no requirement to join גאולה to ערבית.

steps.title: Second explanation: both learn from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now offers the second explanation. Both אמוראים learn from the same פסוק, ״בשכבך ובקומך״. This line sets up the next two steps, which show how each one reads it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it comes from a verse. Both of them learned from one verse, as it is written: ״When you lie down and when you rise.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא switches to the פסוק explanation. It names the shared verse, and this sets up the next two steps, where each side reads it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts night (״בשכבך״) and morning (״ובקומך״) side by side. That suggests the night שמע should be like the morning שמע. The question for the next steps is: like the morning in what way?

keyTerms.meaning: When you lie down and when you rise (from the שמע paragraph)

phrases.english: And if you want, say it comes from a verse,
phrases.notes: The second of the two explanations from step 11.

phrases.english: and both of them learned from one verse,
as it is written: "When you lie down and when you rise."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the סברא explanation and opens the alternative פסוק explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument comes from two different readings of the same verse, ״בשכבך ובקומך״.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: night should follow the morning order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the verse as a הקש comparing night to morning. In the morning we say קריאת שמע and then תפלה, so at night we also say קריאת שמע first and then תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds: the verse compares lying down to rising. Just as when rising, it is קריאת שמע and afterward תפלה, so too when lying down, it is קריאת שמע and afterward תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן reads the verse. Night is compared to morning in the order of שמע and then תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that in the morning שמע comes first and then תפלה. רבי יוחנן uses the הקש to copy that same order to the night. This is exactly the order in the ברייתא of the worker from step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a הקש), linking two things written together so they share a law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds:
the verse compares lying down to rising,

phrases.aramaic: מָה קִימָה — קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ תְּפִלָּה,
phrases.english: just as at rising it is the reading of Shema and afterward prayer,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁכִיבָה נָמֵי — קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וְאַחַר כָּךְ תְּפִלָּה.
phrases.english: so too at lying down, it is the reading of Shema and afterward prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: מַקִּישׁ שְׁכִיבָה לְקִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reading of the verse introduced in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקש copies the morning order (שמע, then תפלה) to the night.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: night שמע should be close to going to bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי uses the same הקש but compares something else. In the morning, שמע is said close to getting out of bed, so at night שמע should be said close to getting into bed. That means one davens first and says שמע last.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי holds: the verse compares lying down to rising. Just as when rising, קריאת שמע is close to one's bed, so too when lying down, קריאת שמע is close to one's bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of the same verse. For him the comparison is about timing: שמע should be said near the bed, both in the morning and at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same הקש. They disagree about what the comparison teaches. רבי יוחנן copies the order of שמע and תפלה. רבי יהושע בן לוי copies the closeness of שמע to the bed. So at night שמע should be the last thing before sleep, which means תפלה comes before it, as in step 9.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי's הקש does not mention תפלה at all. It only says שמע should be near the bed. The ruling that תפלה comes first is a result of this: if שמע must be right before sleep, the davening has to come before it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the argument. (1) סברא: was the night's partial גאולה enough to tie גאולה to ערבית? רבי יוחנן says yes, רבי יהושע בן לוי says no. (2) פסוק: both learn from ״בשכבך ובקומך״. רבי יוחנן copies the morning order (שמע, then תפלה) to the night. רבי יהושע בן לוי copies the morning closeness to the bed, so at night he puts שמע last, after תפלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic example of two אמוראים using the very same הקש but taking a different point of comparison from it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi holds:
the verse compares lying down to rising:

phrases.aramaic: מָה קִימָה — קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע סָמוּךְ לְמִטָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: just as at rising, the reading of Shema is close to his bed,
phrases.notes: In the morning, one says שמע soon after getting up.

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁכִיבָה נָמֵי — קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע סָמוּךְ לְמִטָּתוֹ.
phrases.english: so too at lying down, the reading of Shema is close to his bed.
phrases.notes: So at night, שמע is said last, right before sleep.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי סָבַר: מַקִּישׁ שְׁכִיבָה לְקִימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same הקש, completing the פסוק explanation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הקש compares how close שמע is to the bed. So the night שמע is said right before sleep, after תפלה.

steps.title: The evening blessing השכיבנו seems to separate גאולה from תפלה
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבינא quotes a משנה: at night there are two blessings after שמע. The second one, השכיבנו, stands between the גאולה blessing and the עמידה. So how can רבי יוחנן say we must join them?
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בריה דרבינא raised an objection. The משנה says: at night a person says two blessings before שמע and two blessings after it. Now, if you say a person must join גאולה to תפלה, he is not doing that, because he still has to say השכיבנו in between!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's view using a משנה about the order of the night blessings. The second blessing after שמע seems to block the joining of גאולה and תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that at night, just like in the morning, the גאולה blessing must lead straight into the עמידה. But the משנה lists two blessings after שמע at night: first גאל ישראל (the גאולה blessing), then השכיבנו. So something does come between גאולה and תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
two blessings before שמע and two after it
to join one thing right next to another with no break
'Lay us down in peace', the second blessing after שמע at night

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the first blessing after שמע. That one IS the גאולה blessing. The problem is the second blessing, השכיבנו, which comes after the גאולה blessing and before the עמידה.

phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, raises an objection:
In the evening one recites
phrases.notes: Quoting a later משנה (Berakhot 11a)

phrases.english: two blessings before it and two after it.
And if you say that one must join (redemption to prayer),

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא קָא סָמֵךְ גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה,
phrases.english: then he is not joining redemption to prayer,
since he must still say 'Hashkiveinu' in between!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's position from Step 15, that at night שמע and its גאולה blessing must come right before the עמידה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that one must join גאולה to תפלה at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires השכיבנו after the גאולה blessing. That is an interruption, so joining is impossible at night.

steps.title: השכיבנו counts as part of one long גאולה blessing
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that חז״ל instituted השכיבנו, so it is treated as an extension of the גאולה blessing. It is not a break.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: since the רבנן instituted השכיבנו, it is like one long גאולה blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: השכיבנו is not an interruption. It counts as part of the גאולה blessing itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An interruption is something foreign that comes between two things. Because the רבנן themselves set up השכיבנו in this spot, it is treated as a stretched-out continuation of גאולה, not as a separate break. So רבי יוחנן's rule still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'they say', an unnamed answer from the scholars
it is like, it is considered as

phrases.english: They say (in answer):
since the Rabbis instituted 'Hashkiveinu',
it is considered like one extended redemption blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: the supposed interruption is treated as part of the blessing itself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: השכיבנו is a separate blessing that breaks the link between גאולה and תפלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the רבנן instituted it, השכיבנו is an extension of גאולה, so the link is not broken.

steps.title: Proof from the morning: a verse is said between redemption and prayer there too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports its answer. In the morning, everyone agrees גאולה must be joined to תפלה, yet רבי יוחנן says we say ״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״ before the עמידה. That verse would also be a break unless additions made by חז״ל do not count as breaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, how could anyone join גאולה to תפלה in the morning? רבי יוחנן said: at the beginning of the עמידה one says 'ה׳, open my lips', and at the end one says 'May the words of my mouth be acceptable'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves its answer by pointing to the morning service. It shows we already accept this kind of 'non-interruption' there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the morning both אמוראים agree that גאולה must be joined to תפלה. Yet רבי יוחנן himself adds the פסוק ״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״ between them. If every addition counted as a break, joining would be impossible even in the morning. So the same reasoning has to apply to השכיבנו.

keyTerms.meaning: for if you do not say this (proof that something must be true)
'ה׳, open my lips', the פסוק said before the עמידה
'May the words of my mouth be acceptable', said after the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: Only the opening פסוק (״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״) causes the problem, because it comes between גאולה and the עמידה. The closing פסוק (״יהיו לרצון״) is part of רבי יוחנן's quote, but it is not part of the question.

phrases.english: For if you do not say so,
how can one join (redemption to prayer) in the morning?
But Rabbi Yochanan said:
At the beginning one says: 'Lord, open my lips',
and at the end he says:
'May the words of my mouth be acceptable.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, שַׁחֲרִית הֵיכִי מָצֵי סָמֵיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of Step 18 by showing that the alternative leads to an impossible result in the morning.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that additions instituted by the רבנן do not count as interruptions
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement that ״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״ is said before the עמידה, even in the morning where joining is required

steps.title: Both morning and evening additions are part of the prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes: ״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״ counts as an extended תפלה, and in the same way השכיבנו counts as an extended גאולה. Neither one is an interruption.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there in the morning, since the רבנן instituted saying 'ה׳, open my lips', it is like one long תפלה. Here too, since the רבנן instituted saying השכיבנו, it is like one long גאולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the argument. It applies one rule to both cases: anything the רבנן instituted in that spot becomes part of the blessing next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning פסוק is attached forward, to the עמידה. השכיבנו is attached backward, to גאולה. Either way nothing foreign interrupts, so רבי יוחנן's night rule survives the challenge.
steps.whatToRemember: Words that חז״ל instituted in a specific place are part of the nearby blessing, not an interruption. That is why השכיבנו at night and ״ה׳ שפתי תפתח״ in the morning do not break סמיכת גאולה לתפלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the practice of joining גאולה to תפלה works even with fixed additions. It is the basis for avoiding other interruptions between גאל ישראל and the עמידה.

phrases.english: Rather, there (in the morning),

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּתַקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר ״ה׳ שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח״ —
phrases.english: since the Rabbis instituted saying 'Lord, open my lips',
it is considered like one extended prayer.
Here too (in the evening),
since the Rabbis instituted saying 'Hashkiveinu',
it is considered like one extended redemption blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the morning proof in Step 19 and applies it back to השכיבנו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Additions instituted by the רבנן do not interrupt. השכיבנו is an extended גאולה, so רבי יוחנן's rule of joining גאולה to the evening תפלה stands.

steps.title: Saying תהלה לדוד three times a day earns עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי אבינא, says that anyone who recites תהלה לדוד (אשרי) three times every day is promised a share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אבינא: anyone who says תהלה לדוד three times every day is promised that he is a member of עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new, related teaching. Earlier, joining גאולה to תפלה was linked to earning עולם הבא, and now another practice with the same promise is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic about the special value of תהלה לדוד (תהלים קמ״ה). The promise matches רבי יוחנן's earlier teaching that one who joins גאולה to תפלה is a בן עולם הבא. The next lines of the גמרא will explain why this מזמור in particular is singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: תהלים קמ״ה, the core of אשרי
one who has a share in the World to Come

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for saying אשרי three times a day: twice in שחרית and once in מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Avina:
Anyone who says 'A Psalm of David'
three times every day
is assured
that he is a member of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related topic, linked by the shared theme of being promised עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reciting תהלה לדוד three times daily assures one a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What is special about this chapter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why reciting תהלה לדוד earns such a huge reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why תהלה לדוד, of all the chapters in תהלים, gets the promise of עולם הבא. This question sets up the search for a reason that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step gave a big promise without a reason. The גמרא now wants to know what feature of this chapter makes it more valuable than other chapters of praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Psalm 145, the chapter we call אשרי

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: Why does this particular chapter earn עולם הבא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the promise stated in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What feature of תהלה לדוד makes it worthy of the promise of עולם הבא.

steps.title: First suggestion: because it follows the alphabet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason might be that the chapter is arranged by the אלף בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it goes in order of the alphabet,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer: the verses of תהלה לדוד begin with the letters of the אלף בית in order. The word אילימא tells us this is only a suggestion that is about to be tested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alphabetical chapter is a complete, organized praise of ה׳, from א to ת. That could explain why it is special. The next line will test whether this reason really works.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will likely be rejected)
The alphabet, meaning an alphabetical arrangement

phrases.english: If you say it is because it comes in alphabetical order,
phrases.notes: Each verse of Psalm 145 starts with the next letter of the alphabet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Perhaps the chapter is special because it is arranged alphabetically.

steps.title: Rejected: Psalm 119 goes through the alphabet eight times
steps.stepSummary: If the alphabet were the reason, we should say אשרי תמימי דרך, which has the alphabet eight times over.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us say ״אשרי תמימי דרך״, which comes in eight alphabetical rounds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first suggestion. If the alphabet were the reason, תהלים קי״ט (אשרי תמימי דרך) should be even better, because it goes through the whole alphabet eight times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reason has to explain why this chapter wins over every other chapter. Psalm 119 has more of the alphabet feature, eight verses for each letter. So the alphabet alone cannot be why תהלה לדוד was chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; then we should recite
Eight rounds (eight verses for each letter)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two אשרי's. The chapter we call אשרי is תהלה לדוד (Psalm 145). ״אשרי תמימי דרך״ here is a different chapter, Psalm 119.

phrases.english: Then let us say "Happy are those whose way is perfect"
phrases.notes: Psalm 119

phrases.english: which comes in eight alphabetical rounds.
phrases.notes: Each letter has eight verses, so the alphabet runs eight times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alphabetical suggestion of step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the alphabet as the sole reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another chapter, Psalm 119, has the alphabet feature even more, so this reason does not single out תהלה לדוד.

steps.title: Second suggestion: because of the verse פותח את ידך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason might be the verse praising ה׳ for feeding all living things.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it contains ״You open Your hand.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new reason: תהלה לדוד contains the verse ״פותח את ידך ומשביע לכל חי רצון״, praising ה׳ for feeding every creature. This is again a suggestion that will be tested next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the first reason was dropped and a new one is being offered. Praising ה׳ as the One who feeds the whole world is an important idea, so it could explain the special reward.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and offers a new one)
"You open Your hand": the verse praising ה׳ for feeding all creatures

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״,
phrases.english: Rather, it is because it contains "You open Your hand,"
phrases.notes: Psalm 145:16, ה׳ gives food to every living thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בֵּיהּ ״פּוֹתֵחַ אֶת יָדֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the alphabet reason was rejected in step 24, offers a second possible answer to step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Perhaps the chapter is special because it praises ה׳ for feeding all creatures.

steps.title: Rejected: הלל הגדול also praises ה׳ for giving food
steps.stepSummary: If feeding the world were the reason, we should say הלל הגדול, which has ״נותן לחם לכל בשר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us say הלל הגדול, where it is written ״He gives bread to all flesh.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion. הלל הגדול (Psalm 136) also praises ה׳ for feeding everyone, so it should earn the reward too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the reason does not single out תהלה לדוד, because another chapter has the same praise. So the food verse alone is not enough to explain why this chapter was chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Great Hallel": Psalm 136 (הודו לה׳ כי טוב... כי לעולם חסדו)
"He gives bread to all flesh": a verse in Psalm 136

steps.confusionAlert: הלל הגדול is not the הלל we say on ראש חודש and יום טוב (Psalms 113-118). It is Psalm 136, the chapter where every verse ends ״כי לעולם חסדו״.

phrases.english: Then let us say "the Great Hallel"
phrases.notes: Psalm 136

phrases.english: in which it is written, "He gives bread to all flesh."
phrases.notes: Psalm 136:25, the same idea as פותח את ידך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the food-verse suggestion of step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the food verse as the sole reason.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הלל הגדול also contains praise for ה׳ feeding all creatures, so this reason does not single out תהלה לדוד.

steps.title: Conclusion: it has both features together
steps.stepSummary: תהלה לדוד is special because it has both the alphabet order and the verse about feeding all creatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it contains both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that תהלה לדוד is unique because it combines both features: it is alphabetical and it contains ״פותח את ידך״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each feature alone appears in another chapter, but only תהלה לדוד has both together. That combination is what makes it special and explains the promise of עולם הבא.
steps.whatToRemember: אשרי (תהלה לדוד) is special because it is the one chapter that has both the full alphabet and the praise ״פותח את ידך״. Psalm 119 has only the alphabet, and הלל הגדול has only the food praise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why we say אשרי three times every day in תפלה, and why the verse ״פותח את ידך״ needs special focus when saying it.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because it contains both.
phrases.notes: Both the alphabetical order and ״פותח את ידך״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two rejected suggestions into a single answer that holds up.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תהלה לדוד earns the promise of עולם הבא because it uniquely combines an alphabetical arrangement with praise of ה׳ as the One who feeds all creatures.

steps.title: Why there is no verse for the letter נ in אשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says אשרי skips the letter נ because the famous נ verse speaks of Israel's downfall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why is there no verse starting with נ in אשרי? Because the letter נ recalls the downfall of Israel, as it says: "The virgin of Israel has fallen and will rise no more."
steps.whatsHappening: The conversation about אשרי continues. רבי יוחנן notices that one letter, נ, is missing from the alphabet order, and he explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that אשרי is special because it follows the אלף בית. That makes the missing נ stand out. רבי יוחנן explains that the best-known verse starting with נ, from עמוס, describes Israel falling, so דוד המלך left that letter out to avoid hinting at it.

keyTerms.meaning: תהלים קמ״ה, the psalm called תהלה לדוד
Literally 'enemies of Israel', a polite way of saying Israel itself
The virgin of Israel, a poetic name for the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: "שונאי ישראל" does NOT mean Israel's actual enemies here. It is a polite substitute so the גמרא does not have to say outright that Israel falls. The verse is about Israel itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר נוּן בְּ״אַשְׁרֵי״ —
phrases.english: Why is no verse beginning with nun said in Ashrei?
Because there is in it (the letter nun)
the downfall of the 'enemies of Israel' (a polite way of saying Israel)
phrases.notes: A euphemism for Israel itself

phrases.english: as it is written:
"She has fallen, she will no more rise, the virgin of Israel."
phrases.notes: עמוס ה:ב

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר נוּן בְּ״אַשְׁרֵי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the point that אשרי follows the alphabet by explaining the one letter that is missing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The letter נ is left out of אשרי because the נ verse in עמוס speaks of Israel's downfall.

steps.title: The gentler reading of the verse in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they divided the verse differently so it becomes a message of hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they read it this way: "She has fallen, and she will not fall again. Rise, virgin of Israel!"
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל soften the harsh verse. They change where the sentence breaks so it now promises that Israel will rise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain reading says Israel will "no more rise." By moving the pause, the verse instead says Israel will not fall again, followed by a call to "Rise!" The same words now carry a hopeful meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)

phrases.english: In the West they explain it like this:
"She has fallen, and she will not fall again;
rise, virgin of Israel!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the harsh verse quoted by רבי יוחנן by offering a hopeful reading of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Read with a different pause, the verse means Israel will fall no more and is told to rise.

steps.title: דוד still gave comfort right after the missing נ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that even though דוד left out נ, the very next verse (ס) comforts those who fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Even so, דוד came back and supported them through רוח הקודש, as it says: "ה׳ supports all who fall."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds comfort to רבי יוחנן's idea. Right where the נ verse would have been, the next verse in אשרי lifts up those who fell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד המלך saw through רוח הקודש that עמוס would one day say "נפלה" (she fell). So in the ס verse that comes right after the missing נ, he wrote "סומך ה׳ לכל הנופלים", answering that fall ahead of time.
steps.whatToRemember: אשרי skips נ to avoid hinting at Israel's fall (רבי יוחנן), but the very next verse, סומך ה׳ לכל הנופלים, comforts the fallen (רב נחמן בר יצחק).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains a feature of אשרי that we say three times a day: the missing נ and the comforting ס verse right after it.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Even so (even though nun was left out),
David went back and supported them through divine inspiration,
as it says: "ה׳ supports all who fall."
phrases.notes: תהלים קמ״ה:יד, the ס verse

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: אֲפִילּוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי יוחנן's teaching by showing that דוד also answered the fall in the next verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through רוח הקודש, דוד wrote סומך ה׳ לכל הנופלים in the ס verse to comfort the fall hinted at by the missing נ.

steps.title: מיכאל is described as greater than גבריאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא says מיכאל reached his mission in one flight, while גבריאל needed two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בר אבינא said: What is said about מיכאל is greater than what is said about גבריאל. About מיכאל it says, "One of the שרפים flew to me," but about גבריאל it says, "The man גבריאל, whom I saw in the vision at the beginning, flying, flying..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי אלעזר בר אבינא compares two verses to show that מיכאל is faster than גבריאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מיכאל, the verse says "flew" only once, meaning he arrived in a single flight. With גבריאל, the verse doubles the word ("מועף ביעף"), meaning he needed two flights. Fewer flights shows greater speed and greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: Flying, flying, a doubled word that hints at two flights

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar bar Avina said:
Greater is what is said about Michael
than what is said about Gabriel,
for about Michael it is written:
"And one of the seraphim flew to me."
phrases.notes: ישעיה ו:ו, a single flight

phrases.english: while about Gabriel it is written:
"And the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision
at the beginning, flying swiftly (literally: flown in flight), etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל ט:כא, the doubled word suggests two flights

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר אֲבִינָא: גָּדוֹל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמִיכָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching. It is likely placed here because it comes from a similarly named rabbi as the earlier statements about אשרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מיכאל arrives in one flight and גבריאל in two, so מיכאל is described as greater.

steps.title: How do we know the verse is about מיכאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source showing that "one of the שרפים" refers to מיכאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this "one" is מיכאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check something רבי אלעזר בר אבינא assumed. The verse never names מיכאל, so where do we see that it means him? This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in ישעיה only says "one of the שרפים" and does not give a name. The whole comparison depends on that angel being מיכאל, so the גמרא asks for proof before the teaching can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows, from where is it implied
One, the unnamed angel in the verse

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on רבי אלעזר בר אבינא. It is a genuine request for the source of his assumption, and the answer comes next.

phrases.english: From where is it implied
that this "one" is Michael?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of an assumption built into רבי אלעזר בר אבינא's comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the unnamed "one of the שרפים" in ישעיה is מיכאל.

steps.title: The word 'אחד' links the שרף to מיכאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers the question from Step 32 with a גזירה שוה. The word 'אחד' appears both in ישעיהו about the שרף and in דניאל about מיכאל, so the two refer to the same angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We learn it from 'one' and 'one.' Here it says, 'And one of the seraphim flew to me,' and there it says, 'And behold, מיכאל, one of the chief princes, came to help me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: how do we know the flying angel in ישעיהו is מיכאל? רבי יוחנן matches a shared word in two verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, the verse openly names מיכאל and calls him 'אחד.' Since ישעיהו also uses 'אחד' for the שרף, the shared word lets us identify that שרף as מיכאל too. This supports רבי אלעזר בר אבינא's claim from Step 31 that מיכאל flew in one flight.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes (is learned) from, the opening word of a גזירה שוה
It is written here... and it is written there, the standard way a word-link is laid out
Seraphim, a type of fiery angel
The chief princes, the top-ranking angels

steps.confusionAlert: 'אחד' here does not only mean the number one. It is being read as a hint to a specific, outstanding angel. It is the shared word that matters for the proof, not the counting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is learned from 'one' and 'one.'
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה: the same word in two verses links them.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'And there flew to me'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 6:6

phrases.english: one of the seraphim,'
and it is written there: 'And behold, Michael,'
phrases.notes: דניאל 10:13

phrases.english: one of the chief princes
came to help me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'אחד' between ישעיהו 6:6 and דניאל 10:13 identifies the שרף as מיכאל.

steps.title: Ranking messengers by number of flights
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists how many flights each heavenly messenger needs: מיכאל one, גבריאל two, אליהו four, מלאך המות eight. During a plague, מלאך המות arrives in one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: מיכאל arrives in one flight, גבריאל in two, אליהו in four, and מלאך המות in eight. But in a time of plague, he arrives in one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that expands on רבי אלעזר בר אבינא's idea into a full list of who travels fastest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of flights shows rank and speed. מיכאל, the angel of kindness, comes fastest, and מלאך המות comes slowest, which hints that ה׳'s kindness comes quickly and punishment comes slowly. The plague exception shows that when judgment is decreed, death can come very quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught, introducing a ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים)

steps.whatToRemember: The angel discussion closes here: מיכאל is fastest, and מלאך המות is slowest, except during a plague.

phrases.english: It was taught: Michael, in one (flight);
Gabriel, in two;
Elijah, in four;
and the Angel of Death, in eight.
But in a time of plague, in one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the מיכאל/גבריאל comparison with a fuller list from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Messengers are ranked by flights: מיכאל 1, גבריאל 2, אליהו 4, מלאך המות 8, but only 1 during a plague.

steps.title: Saying שמע again in bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי rules that even if a person already said קריאת שמע in shul, there is a מצוה to say it again on his bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Even though a person said קריאת שמע in shul, it is a מצוה to say it again on his bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the angel topic and returns to the main subject of the פרק, the evening קריאת שמע. A new rule is given about saying שמע at bedtime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though שמע was already said in shul, there is still a מצוה to say it again in bed, right before sleep. The shul reading does not replace the bedtime reading. רש״י explains that the shul שמע was often said before nightfall, too early to count, so the bedtime שמע is the main one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for קריאת שמע על המטה, the bedtime שמע that is said in practice.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Even though a person has read
the Shema in the synagogue,
it is a מצוה to read it on his bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּרָא אָדָם קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: back to קריאת שמע after the long אגדה about אשרי and angels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after saying שמע in shul, there is a מצוה to say it again on one's bed.

steps.title: A verse supporting שמע in bed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings a verse from תהלים: 'Speak in your hearts on your beds and be still.' It hints at saying שמע in bed and then going to sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: What is the verse? 'Tremble and do not sin; speak in your hearts on your beds, and be still, סלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives a verse to support רבי יהושע בן לוי's bedtime-שמע rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Speak in your hearts' hints at שמע, which says 'על לבבך' (on your heart). 'On your beds' tells us where to say it, and 'be still' means to then go quietly to sleep. So the verse matches the order: say שמע in bed, then sleep.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for a scriptural source)
And be still, סלה (then go to sleep)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: What is the verse?
'Tremble and do not sin;'
phrases.notes: תהלים 4:5

phrases.english: speak in your hearts on your beds,
phrases.notes: 'In your hearts' hints to שמע ('על לבבך').

phrases.english: and be still, Selah.'
phrases.notes: After saying שמע, go quietly to sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a verse to support the rule in Step 35.
steps.raayaObject: The מצוה to say קריאת שמע on one's bed
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 4:5, 'אמרו בלבבכם על משכבכם ודמו סלה'

steps.title: רב נחמן begins a comment
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן starts a statement about the bedtime שמע rule. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line: the גמרא introduces רב נחמן, and his actual statement comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is taught yet. This line opens רב נחמן's response to the rule of רבי יהושע בן לוי, so the learner should expect a comment or condition on the bedtime שמע next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from בבל, about to comment on the bedtime שמע

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a further comment on the rule of Step 35. The comment itself is on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attribution only. The content follows on the next amud.
